blocks.en_text: I have a confession to make.
blocks.zh_text: 我得坦白一件事。

blocks.en_text: But first, I want you to make a little confession to me.
blocks.zh_text: 但首先，我想让你们也向我坦白一点。

blocks.en_text: In the past year, I want you to just raise your hand
blocks.zh_text: 在过去一年里，如果你感受到的压力相对较小，请举手。

blocks.en_text: if you've experienced relatively little stress.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你在过去一年里感受到的压力相对较小，请举手。

blocks.en_text: Anyone?
blocks.zh_text: 有人吗？

blocks.en_text: How about a moderate amount of stress?
blocks.zh_text: 那压力适中的人呢？

blocks.en_text: Who has experienced a lot of stress?
blocks.zh_text: 谁经历过很大的压力？

blocks.en_text: Yeah. Me too.
blocks.zh_text: 对，我也是。

blocks.en_text: But that is not my confession.
blocks.zh_text: 但这还不是我要坦白的事。

blocks.en_text: My confession is this:
blocks.zh_text: 我要坦白的是：

blocks.en_text: I am a health psychologist,
blocks.zh_text: 我是一名健康心理学家，

blocks.en_text: and my mission is to help people be happier and healthier.
blocks.zh_text: 我的使命是帮助人们更快乐、更健康。

blocks.en_text: But I fear that something I've been teaching
blocks.zh_text: 但我担心，我过去10年来一直在教的东西，弊大于利，

blocks.en_text: for the last 10 years is doing more harm than good,
blocks.zh_text: 我担心我过去10年来一直在教的东西，弊大于利，

blocks.en_text: and it has to do with stress.
blocks.zh_text: 而这和压力有关。

blocks.en_text: For years I've been telling people, stress makes you sick.
blocks.zh_text: 多年来我一直告诉人们，压力会让你生病。

blocks.en_text: It increases the risk of everything from the common cold
blocks.zh_text: 它会增加各种疾病的风险，从普通感冒

blocks.en_text: to cardiovascular disease.
blocks.zh_text: 到心血管疾病。

blocks.en_text: Basically, I've turned stress into the enemy.
blocks.zh_text: 基本上，我把压力变成了敌人。

blocks.en_text: But I have changed my mind about stress,
blocks.zh_text: 但我已经改变了对压力的看法，

blocks.en_text: and today, I want to change yours.
blocks.zh_text: 而今天，我想改变你们的看法。

blocks.en_text: Let me start with the study that made me rethink
blocks.zh_text: 让我从一项研究说起，它让我重新思考

blocks.en_text: my whole approach to stress.
blocks.zh_text: 我对待压力的整个方式。

blocks.en_text: This study tracked 30,000 adults in the United States for eight years,
blocks.zh_text: 这项研究追踪了美国3万名成年人，历时八年，

blocks.en_text: and they started by asking people,
blocks.zh_text: 他们一开始先问人们：

blocks.en_text: "How much stress have you experienced in the last year?"
blocks.zh_text: “过去一年里你经历了多少压力？”

blocks.en_text: They also asked,
blocks.zh_text: 他们还问：

blocks.en_text: "Do you believe that stress is harmful for your health?"
blocks.zh_text: “你认为压力对你的健康有害吗？”

blocks.en_text: And then they used public death records to find out who died.
blocks.zh_text: 然后他们用公开的死亡记录来查明谁去世了。

blocks.en_text: Okay.
blocks.zh_text: 好。

blocks.en_text: Some bad news first.
blocks.zh_text: 先说一些坏消息。

blocks.en_text: People who experienced a lot of stress in the previous year
blocks.zh_text: 过去一年里经历过大量压力的人，

blocks.en_text: had a 43 percent increased risk of dying.
blocks.zh_text: 死亡风险增加了43%。

blocks.en_text: But that was only true for the people
blocks.zh_text: 但这只适用于那些人——

blocks.en_text: who also believed that stress is harmful for your health.
blocks.zh_text: 他们也认为压力对健康有害。

blocks.en_text: People who experienced a lot of stress
blocks.zh_text: 那些经历过大量压力

blocks.en_text: but did not view stress as harmful
blocks.zh_text: 但不认为压力有害的人，

blocks.en_text: were no more likely to die.
blocks.zh_text: 死亡的可能性并没有更高。

blocks.en_text: In fact, they had the lowest risk of dying
blocks.zh_text: 事实上，他们的死亡风险是最低的，

blocks.en_text: of anyone in the study,
blocks.zh_text: 是研究中所有人里最低的，

blocks.en_text: including people who had relatively little stress.
blocks.zh_text: 包括那些压力相对较小的人。

blocks.en_text: Now the researchers estimated that over the eight years
blocks.zh_text: 现在，研究人员估计，在他们追踪死亡情况的八年里，

blocks.en_text: they were tracking deaths,
blocks.zh_text: 在他们追踪死亡情况的八年里，

blocks.en_text: 182,000 Americans died prematurely,
blocks.zh_text: 有18.2万美国人过早死亡，

blocks.en_text: not from stress,
blocks.zh_text: 不是死于压力，

blocks.en_text: but from the belief that stress is bad for you.
blocks.zh_text: 而是死于“压力对你有害”这个信念。

blocks.en_text: That is over 20,000 deaths a year.
blocks.zh_text: 这相当于每年超过2万人死亡。

blocks.en_text: Now, if that estimate is correct,
blocks.zh_text: 如果这个估计是正确的，

blocks.en_text: that would make believing stress is bad for you
blocks.zh_text: 那么“认为压力对你有害”这一信念

blocks.en_text: the 15th largest cause of death in the United States last year,
blocks.zh_text: 就会成为去年美国第15大死因，

blocks.en_text: killing more people than skin cancer, HIV/AIDS and homicide.
blocks.zh_text: 致死人数超过皮肤癌、艾滋病和凶杀。

blocks.en_text: You can see why this study freaked me out.
blocks.zh_text: 你能看出来，为什么这项研究把我吓坏了。

blocks.en_text: Here I've been spending so much energy telling people
blocks.zh_text: 我一直以来花了那么多精力去告诉人们

blocks.en_text: stress is bad for your health.
blocks.zh_text: 压力对健康有害。

blocks.en_text: So this study got me wondering:
blocks.zh_text: 所以这项研究让我不禁想问：

blocks.en_text: Can changing how you think about stress make you healthier?
blocks.zh_text: 改变你对压力的看法，能让你更健康吗？

blocks.en_text: And here the science says yes.
blocks.zh_text: 而在这里，科学给出的答案是肯定的。

blocks.en_text: When you change your mind about stress,
blocks.zh_text: 当你改变对压力的看法时，

blocks.en_text: you can change your body's response to stress.
blocks.zh_text: 你就能改变身体对压力的反应。

blocks.en_text: Now to explain how this works,
blocks.zh_text: 现在，为了解释这是怎么运作的，

blocks.en_text: I want you all to pretend that you are participants
blocks.zh_text: 我想请大家假装自己是参与者，

blocks.en_text: in a study designed to stress you out.
blocks.zh_text: 参加一项专门让你感到压力的研究。

blocks.en_text: It's called the social stress test.
blocks.zh_text: 它叫做社会压力测试。

blocks.en_text: You come into the laboratory,
blocks.zh_text: 你走进实验室，

blocks.en_text: and you're told you have to give
blocks.zh_text: 然后有人告诉你，你得

blocks.en_text: a five-minute impromptu speech on your personal weaknesses
blocks.zh_text: 就自己的个人弱点做一个五分钟的即兴演讲，

blocks.en_text: to a panel of expert evaluators sitting right in front of you,
blocks.zh_text: 讲给坐在你正前方的一排专家评审听，

blocks.en_text: and to make sure you feel the pressure,
blocks.zh_text: 而且为了确保你感受到压力，

blocks.en_text: there are bright lights and a camera in your face,
blocks.zh_text: 还有刺眼的灯光和怼在你脸上的摄像机，

blocks.en_text: kind of like this.
blocks.zh_text: 差不多就像这样。

blocks.en_text: And the evaluators have been trained
blocks.zh_text: 而这些评审都受过训练，

blocks.en_text: to give you discouraging, non-verbal feedback,
blocks.zh_text: 会给你令人泄气的非语言反馈，

blocks.en_text: like this.
blocks.zh_text: 就像这样。

blocks.en_text: (Exhales)
blocks.zh_text: （呼气）

blocks.en_text: Now that you're sufficiently demoralized,
blocks.zh_text: 现在你已经足够灰心丧气了，

blocks.en_text: time for part two: a math test.
blocks.zh_text: 该进行第二部分了：数学测试。

blocks.en_text: And unbeknownst to you,
blocks.zh_text: 而你并不知道，

blocks.en_text: the experimenter has been trained to harass you during it.
blocks.zh_text: 实验者已经受过训练，会在这过程中不断骚扰你。

blocks.en_text: Now we're going to all do this together.
blocks.zh_text: 现在我们要一起来做这个。

blocks.en_text: It's going to be fun.
blocks.zh_text: 会很好玩的。

blocks.en_text: For me.
blocks.zh_text: 对我来说。

blocks.en_text: Okay.
blocks.zh_text: 好。

blocks.en_text: I want you all to count backwards from 996
blocks.zh_text: 我想请大家从996开始倒着数，

blocks.en_text: in increments of seven.
blocks.zh_text: 每次减七。

blocks.en_text: You're going to do this out loud,
blocks.zh_text: 你们要大声地数出来，

blocks.en_text: as fast as you can,
blocks.zh_text: 尽可能快，

blocks.en_text: starting with 996.
blocks.zh_text: 从996开始。

blocks.en_text: Go!
blocks.zh_text: 开始！

blocks.en_text: (Audience counting)
blocks.zh_text: （观众数数）

blocks.en_text: Go faster. Faster please.
blocks.zh_text: 快一点。请再快一点。

blocks.en_text: You're going too slow.
blocks.zh_text: 你数得太慢了。

blocks.en_text: (Audience counting)
blocks.zh_text: （观众数数）

blocks.en_text: Stop. Stop, stop, stop.
blocks.zh_text: 停。停，停，停。

blocks.en_text: That guy made a mistake.
blocks.zh_text: 那个人数错了。

blocks.en_text: We are going to have to start all over again.
blocks.zh_text: 我们得从头再来一遍。

blocks.en_text: You're not very good at this, are you?
blocks.zh_text: 你不太擅长这个，是吧？

blocks.en_text: Okay, so you get the idea.
blocks.zh_text: 好，所以你们明白意思了。

blocks.en_text: If you were actually in this study,
blocks.zh_text: 如果你真的参加了这项研究，

blocks.en_text: you'd probably be a little stressed out.
blocks.zh_text: 你大概会有点压力。

blocks.en_text: Your heart might be pounding,
blocks.zh_text: 你的心可能怦怦直跳，

blocks.en_text: you might be breathing faster, maybe breaking out into a sweat.
blocks.zh_text: 你可能呼吸变快，也许还会冒汗。

blocks.en_text: And normally, we interpret these physical changes as anxiety
blocks.zh_text: 通常，我们会把这些身体变化解读为焦虑，

blocks.en_text: or signs that we aren't coping very well with the pressure.
blocks.zh_text: 或者是我们没能很好应对压力的迹象。

blocks.en_text: But what if you viewed them instead
blocks.zh_text: 但如果你换个角度，把它们看作

blocks.en_text: as signs that your body was energized,
blocks.zh_text: 你的身体充满活力的信号，

blocks.en_text: was preparing you to meet this challenge?
blocks.zh_text: 是在让你做好准备迎接这个挑战呢？

blocks.en_text: Now that is exactly what participants were told
blocks.zh_text: 而这正是参与者被告知的内容，

blocks.en_text: in a study conducted at Harvard University.
blocks.zh_text: 在一项哈佛大学进行的研究中。

blocks.en_text: Before they went through the social stress test,
blocks.zh_text: 在他们经历社会压力测试之前，

blocks.en_text: they were taught to rethink their stress response as helpful.
blocks.zh_text: 他们被教导要把自己的压力反应重新理解为有益的。

blocks.en_text: That pounding heart is preparing you for action.
blocks.zh_text: 那颗怦怦直跳的心脏正在为你行动做准备。

blocks.en_text: If you're breathing faster, it's no problem.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你呼吸变快了，那也没问题。

blocks.en_text: It's getting more oxygen to your brain.
blocks.zh_text: 它是在给大脑输送更多氧气。

blocks.en_text: And participants who learned to view the stress response
blocks.zh_text: 而那些学会了把压力反应

blocks.en_text: as helpful for their performance,
blocks.zh_text: 看作对表现有帮助的参与者，

blocks.en_text: well, they were less stressed out, less anxious, more confident,
blocks.zh_text: 他们压力更小、更不焦虑、更自信，

blocks.en_text: but the most fascinating finding to me
blocks.zh_text: 但对我来说最有趣的发现

blocks.en_text: was how their physical stress response changed.
blocks.zh_text: 是他们的身体压力反应发生了怎样的变化。

blocks.en_text: Now, in a typical stress response,
blocks.zh_text: 在典型的压力反应中，

blocks.en_text: your heart rate goes up,
blocks.zh_text: 你的心率会上升，

blocks.en_text: and your blood vessels constrict like this.
blocks.zh_text: 你的血管会像这样收缩。

blocks.en_text: And this is one of the reasons that chronic stress
blocks.zh_text: 这也是长期压力

blocks.en_text: is sometimes associated with cardiovascular disease.
blocks.zh_text: 有时与心血管疾病有关的原因之一。

blocks.en_text: It's not really healthy to be in this state all the time.
blocks.zh_text: 一直处于这种状态其实并不健康。

blocks.en_text: But in the study,
blocks.zh_text: 但在这项研究中，

blocks.en_text: when participants viewed their stress response as helpful,
blocks.zh_text: 当参与者把压力反应看作有帮助时，

blocks.en_text: their blood vessels stayed relaxed like this.
blocks.zh_text: 他们的血管就像这样保持放松。

blocks.en_text: Their heart was still pounding,
blocks.zh_text: 他们的心脏依然在怦怦跳，

blocks.en_text: but this is a much healthier cardiovascular profile.
blocks.zh_text: 但这是健康得多的心血管状态。

blocks.en_text: It actually looks a lot like what happens
blocks.zh_text: 它实际上看起来很像

blocks.en_text: in moments of joy and courage.
blocks.zh_text: 在喜悦和勇气时刻发生的情况。

blocks.en_text: Over a lifetime of stressful experiences,
blocks.zh_text: 在一生的压力经历中，

blocks.en_text: this one biological change
blocks.zh_text: 这一个生理上的变化

blocks.en_text: could be the difference
blocks.zh_text: 可能就决定了

blocks.en_text: between a stress-induced heart attack at age 50
blocks.zh_text: 是50岁时因压力诱发心脏病发作，

blocks.en_text: and living well into your 90s.
blocks.zh_text: 还是健康活到90多岁。

blocks.en_text: And this is really what the new science of stress reveals,
blocks.zh_text: 而这正是压力新科学所揭示的，

blocks.en_text: that how you think about stress matters.
blocks.zh_text: 你怎么看待压力很重要。

blocks.en_text: So my goal as a health psychologist has changed.
blocks.zh_text: 所以作为一名健康心理学家，我的目标变了。

blocks.en_text: I no longer want to get rid of your stress.
blocks.zh_text: 我不再想消除你的压力。

blocks.en_text: I want to make you better at stress.
blocks.zh_text: 我想让你更擅长应对压力。

blocks.en_text: And we just did a little intervention.
blocks.zh_text: 我们刚刚做了一个小小的干预。

blocks.en_text: If you raised your hand and said
blocks.zh_text: 如果你刚才举手说

blocks.en_text: you'd had a lot of stress in the last year,
blocks.zh_text: 过去一年里你压力很大，

blocks.en_text: we could have saved your life,
blocks.zh_text: 我们可能已经救了你的命，

blocks.en_text: because hopefully the next time your heart is pounding from stress,
blocks.zh_text: 因为希望下次你的心脏因压力而怦怦跳时，

blocks.en_text: you're going to remember this talk
blocks.zh_text: 你会想起这场演讲，

blocks.en_text: and you're going to think to yourself,
blocks.zh_text: 你会对自己说，

blocks.en_text: this is my body helping me rise to this challenge.
blocks.zh_text: 这是我的身体在帮我迎接这个挑战。

blocks.en_text: And when you view stress in that way,
blocks.zh_text: 当你这样看待压力时，

blocks.en_text: your body believes you,
blocks.zh_text: 你的身体会相信你，

blocks.en_text: and your stress response becomes healthier.
blocks.zh_text: 你的压力反应就会变得更健康。

blocks.en_text: Now I said I have over a decade of demonizing stress
blocks.zh_text: 我说过，我花了十多年把压力妖魔化，

blocks.en_text: to redeem myself from,
blocks.zh_text: 需要为自己赎罪，

blocks.en_text: so we are going to do one more intervention.
blocks.zh_text: 所以我们再来做一次干预。

blocks.en_text: I want to tell you
blocks.zh_text: 我想告诉你们

blocks.en_text: about one of the most under-appreciated aspects of the stress response,
blocks.zh_text: 压力反应中最被低估的一个方面，

blocks.en_text: and the idea is this:
blocks.zh_text: 这个观点就是：

blocks.en_text: Stress makes you social.
blocks.zh_text: 压力让你更善于社交。

blocks.en_text: To understand this side of stress,
blocks.zh_text: 要理解压力的这一面，

blocks.en_text: we need to talk about a hormone, oxytocin,
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要谈谈一种激素——催产素。

blocks.en_text: and I know oxytocin has already gotten as much hype as a hormone can get.
blocks.zh_text: 我知道催产素作为一种激素，已经被炒得够火的了。

blocks.en_text: It even has its own cute nickname, the cuddle hormone,
blocks.zh_text: 它甚至有个可爱的昵称，叫“拥抱激素”，

blocks.en_text: because it's released when you hug someone.
blocks.zh_text: 因为你拥抱别人的时候它就会释放。

blocks.en_text: But this is a very small part of what oxytocin is involved in.
blocks.zh_text: 但这只是催产素所参与的一小部分。

blocks.en_text: Oxytocin is a neuro-hormone.
blocks.zh_text: 催产素是一种神经激素。

blocks.en_text: It fine-tunes your brain's social instincts.
blocks.zh_text: 它会微调你大脑的社交本能。

blocks.en_text: It primes you to do things
blocks.zh_text: 它会促使你去做一些

blocks.en_text: that strengthen close relationships.
blocks.zh_text: 能巩固亲密关系的事。

blocks.en_text: Oxytocin makes you crave physical contact with your friends and family.
blocks.zh_text: 催产素会让你渴望和朋友、家人有身体接触。

blocks.en_text: It enhances your empathy.
blocks.zh_text: 它会增强你的共情能力。

blocks.en_text: It even makes you more willing to help and support
blocks.zh_text: 它甚至会让你更愿意去帮助和支持

blocks.en_text: the people you care about.
blocks.zh_text: 你在乎的人。

blocks.en_text: Some people have even suggested we should snort oxytocin...
blocks.zh_text: 有些人甚至建议我们应该吸催产素……

blocks.en_text: to become more compassionate and caring.
blocks.zh_text: 好让自己变得更有同情心、更关心他人。

blocks.en_text: But here's what most people don't understand about oxytocin.
blocks.zh_text: 但关于催产素，大多数人都不了解的是：

blocks.en_text: It's a stress hormone.
blocks.zh_text: 它是一种压力激素。

blocks.en_text: Your pituitary gland pumps this stuff out
blocks.zh_text: 你的脑垂体分泌出这种东西，

blocks.en_text: as part of the stress response.
blocks.zh_text: 作为压力反应的一部分。

blocks.en_text: It's as much a part of your stress response
blocks.zh_text: 它和让你心跳加速的肾上腺素一样，

blocks.en_text: as the adrenaline that makes your heart pound.
blocks.zh_text: 都是你压力反应的一部分。

blocks.en_text: And when oxytocin is released in the stress response,
blocks.zh_text: 而当催产素在压力反应中被释放出来时，

blocks.en_text: it is motivating you to seek support.
blocks.zh_text: 它会促使你去寻求支持。

blocks.en_text: Your biological stress response
blocks.zh_text: 你身体的压力反应

blocks.en_text: is nudging you to tell someone how you feel,
blocks.zh_text: 在轻轻推着你去告诉别人你的感受，

blocks.en_text: instead of bottling it up.
blocks.zh_text: 而不是把情绪憋在心里。

blocks.en_text: Your stress response wants to make sure you notice
blocks.zh_text: 你的压力反应想确保你能注意到

blocks.en_text: when someone else in your life is struggling
blocks.zh_text: 你生活中有人正在苦苦挣扎，

blocks.en_text: so that you can support each other.
blocks.zh_text: 这样你们就能互相支持。

blocks.en_text: When life is difficult,
blocks.zh_text: 当生活艰难时，

blocks.en_text: your stress response wants you to be surrounded
blocks.zh_text: 你的压力反应希望你身边围绕着

blocks.en_text: by people who care about you.
blocks.zh_text: 关心你的人。

blocks.en_text: Okay, so how is knowing this side of stress going to make you healthier?
blocks.zh_text: 好，那么了解压力的这一面，怎么会让你更健康呢？

blocks.en_text: Well, oxytocin doesn't only act on your brain.
blocks.zh_text: 其实，催产素不只作用于你的大脑。

blocks.en_text: It also acts on your body,
blocks.zh_text: 它也作用于你的身体，

blocks.en_text: and one of its main roles in your body
blocks.zh_text: 它在身体里的主要作用之一

blocks.en_text: is to protect your cardiovascular system from the effects of stress.
blocks.zh_text: 就是保护你的心血管系统免受压力的影响。

blocks.en_text: It's a natural anti-inflammatory.
blocks.zh_text: 它是一种天然的消炎物质。

blocks.en_text: It also helps your blood vessels stay relaxed during stress.
blocks.zh_text: 它还能帮助你的血管在压力下保持放松。

blocks.en_text: But my favorite effect on the body is actually on the heart.
blocks.zh_text: 但我最喜欢的它对身体的作用，其实是在心脏上。

blocks.en_text: Your heart has receptors for this hormone,
blocks.zh_text: 你的心脏有这种激素的受体，

blocks.en_text: and oxytocin helps heart cells regenerate
blocks.zh_text: 催产素能帮助心脏细胞再生，

blocks.en_text: and heal from any stress-induced damage.
blocks.zh_text: 并修复任何由压力造成的损伤。

blocks.en_text: This stress hormone strengthens your heart.
blocks.zh_text: 这种压力激素会强健你的心脏。

blocks.en_text: And the cool thing is that all of these physical benefits
blocks.zh_text: 而最妙的是，催产素的这些身体益处

blocks.en_text: of oxytocin are enhanced by social contact and social support.
blocks.zh_text: 都会因社交接触和社交支持而增强。

blocks.en_text: So when you reach out to others under stress,
blocks.zh_text: 所以当你在压力下主动联系他人时，

blocks.en_text: either to seek support or to help someone else,
blocks.zh_text: 无论是寻求支持还是去帮助别人，

blocks.en_text: you release more of this hormone,
blocks.zh_text: 你都会释放更多这种激素，

blocks.en_text: your stress response becomes healthier,
blocks.zh_text: 你的压力反应就会变得更健康，

blocks.en_text: and you actually recover faster from stress.
blocks.zh_text: 而且你实际上能更快地从压力中恢复过来。

blocks.en_text: I find this amazing,
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得这太神奇了，

blocks.en_text: that your stress response has a built-in mechanism
blocks.zh_text: 你的压力反应里竟然有一个内置的机制

blocks.en_text: for stress resilience,
blocks.zh_text: 用来产生抗压韧性，

blocks.en_text: and that mechanism is human connection.
blocks.zh_text: 而这个机制就是人与人之间的联结。

blocks.en_text: I want to finish by telling you about one more study.
blocks.zh_text: 最后，我想再给你们讲一项研究。

blocks.en_text: And listen up, because this study could also save a life.
blocks.zh_text: 请仔细听，因为这项研究也可能救一条命。

blocks.en_text: This study tracked about 1,000 adults in the United States,
blocks.zh_text: 这项研究追踪了美国大约1000名成年人，

blocks.en_text: and they ranged in age from 34 to 93,
blocks.zh_text: 他们的年龄从34岁到93岁不等，

blocks.en_text: and they started the study by asking,
blocks.zh_text: 研究一开始先问他们：

blocks.en_text: "How much stress have you experienced in the last year?"
blocks.zh_text: “过去一年里你经历了多少压力？”

blocks.en_text: They also asked,
blocks.zh_text: 他们还问了：

blocks.en_text: "How much time have you spent helping out friends, neighbors,
blocks.zh_text: “你花了多少时间去帮助朋友、邻居，

blocks.en_text: people in your community?"
blocks.zh_text: 以及你社区里的人？”

blocks.en_text: And then they used public records for the next five years
blocks.zh_text: 然后他们查阅了接下来五年的公开记录，

blocks.en_text: to find out who died.
blocks.zh_text: 看看谁去世了。

blocks.en_text: Okay, so the bad news first:
blocks.zh_text: 好，先说坏消息：

blocks.en_text: For every major stressful life experience,
blocks.zh_text: 每经历一次重大的压力性生活事件，

blocks.en_text: like financial difficulties or family crisis,
blocks.zh_text: 比如经济困难或家庭危机，

blocks.en_text: that increased the risk of dying by 30 percent.
blocks.zh_text: 死亡风险就会增加30%。

blocks.en_text: But -- and I hope you are expecting a "but" by now --
blocks.zh_text: 但是——我猜你们现在已经料到会有个“但是”了——

blocks.en_text: but that wasn't true for everyone.
blocks.zh_text: 但并不是所有人都这样。

blocks.en_text: People who spent time caring for others
blocks.zh_text: 那些花时间照顾他人的人

blocks.en_text: showed absolutely no stress-related increase in dying.
blocks.zh_text: 完全没有出现与压力相关的死亡风险上升。

blocks.en_text: Zero.
blocks.zh_text: 一点都没有。

blocks.en_text: Caring created resilience.
blocks.zh_text: 关爱他人造就了韧性。

blocks.en_text: And so we see once again
blocks.zh_text: 于是我们再一次看到，

blocks.en_text: that the harmful effects of stress on your health
blocks.zh_text: 压力对健康的有害影响

blocks.en_text: are not inevitable.
blocks.zh_text: 并不是不可避免的。

blocks.en_text: How you think and how you act
blocks.zh_text: 你如何思考、如何行动，

blocks.en_text: can transform your experience of stress.
blocks.zh_text: 能够改变你经历压力的方式。

blocks.en_text: When you choose to view your stress response as helpful,
blocks.zh_text: 当你选择把自己的压力反应看作是有帮助的，

blocks.en_text: you create the biology of courage.
blocks.zh_text: 你就创造出了勇气的生理机制。

blocks.en_text: And when you choose to connect with others under stress,
blocks.zh_text: 而当你选择在压力下与他人建立联结，

blocks.en_text: you can create resilience.
blocks.zh_text: 你就能创造出韧性。

blocks.en_text: Now I wouldn't necessarily ask for more stressful experiences in my life,
blocks.zh_text: 当然，我不会主动要求自己的生活里多一些压力体验，

blocks.en_text: but this science has given me a whole new appreciation for stress.
blocks.zh_text: 但这门科学让我对压力有了全新的认识。

blocks.en_text: Stress gives us access to our hearts.
blocks.zh_text: 压力让我们触及自己的内心。

blocks.en_text: The compassionate heart that finds joy and meaning
blocks.zh_text: 那颗充满同情的心，能在与他人联结中找到快乐和意义，

blocks.en_text: in connecting with others,
blocks.zh_text: 与他人建立联结中找到快乐和意义，

blocks.en_text: and yes, your pounding physical heart,
blocks.zh_text: 没错，还有你那颗砰砰跳动的心脏，

blocks.en_text: working so hard to give you strength and energy.
blocks.zh_text: 它如此努力地工作，给你力量和能量。

blocks.en_text: And when you choose to view stress in this way,
blocks.zh_text: 而当你选择以这种方式看待压力时，

blocks.en_text: you're not just getting better at stress,
blocks.zh_text: 你不仅是在压力面前变得更从容，

blocks.en_text: you're actually making a pretty profound statement.
blocks.zh_text: 你实际上是在表达一个相当深刻的宣言。

blocks.en_text: You're saying that you can trust yourself to handle life's challenges.
blocks.zh_text: 你在说，你相信自己能够应对生活中的挑战。

blocks.en_text: And you're remembering that you don't have to face them alone.
blocks.zh_text: 而且你记得，你不必独自面对它们。

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢。

blocks.en_text: Chris Anderson: This is kind of amazing, what you're telling us.
blocks.zh_text: Chris Anderson：你告诉我们的这些真有点不可思议。

blocks.en_text: It seems amazing to me that a belief about stress
blocks.zh_text: 对我来说很神奇的是，一个关于压力的信念

blocks.en_text: can make so much difference to someone's life expectancy.
blocks.zh_text: 竟然能对一个人的预期寿命产生这么大的影响。

blocks.en_text: How would that extend to advice,
blocks.zh_text: 那这该怎么延伸到建议上呢？

blocks.en_text: like, if someone is making a lifestyle choice
blocks.zh_text: 比如说，如果有人在做一个生活方式上的选择

blocks.en_text: between, say, a stressful job and a non-stressful job,
blocks.zh_text: 在比如一份压力大的工作和一份压力小的工作之间选，

blocks.en_text: does it matter which way they go?
blocks.zh_text: 他们选哪边有关系吗？

blocks.en_text: It's equally wise to go for the stressful job
blocks.zh_text: 选择压力大的那份工作同样也是明智的，

blocks.en_text: so long as you believe that you can handle it, in some sense?
blocks.zh_text: 只要你在某种意义上相信自己能应付得了？

blocks.en_text: KM: Yeah, and one thing we know for certain
blocks.zh_text: KM：是的，而且有一件事我们很确定，

blocks.en_text: is that chasing meaning is better for your health
blocks.zh_text: 那就是追求意义对你的健康更有好处，

blocks.en_text: than trying to avoid discomfort.
blocks.zh_text: 比试图逃避不适要好。

blocks.en_text: And so I would say that's really the best way to make decisions,
blocks.zh_text: 所以我会说，那才是做决定的最好方式，

blocks.en_text: is go after what it is that creates meaning in your life
blocks.zh_text: 就是去追求那些能为你的人生创造意义的东西，

blocks.en_text: and then trust yourself to handle the stress that follows.
blocks.zh_text: 然后相信自己能应对随之而来的压力。

blocks.en_text: CA: Thank you so much, Kelly. It's pretty cool.
blocks.zh_text: CA：非常感谢你，Kelly。这真的很棒。
